nom: EltaMD UV Sheer Face and Body Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily or oil-prone skin get mixed results: one with an oil-prone T-zone says it leaves her looking like 'a ball of grease' within an hour despite claims of a non-greasy finish, while several other reviewers recommend it specifically for oily skin types.
segments.dry: The one reviewer identifying as dry-skinned found the lightweight fluid didn't feel like enough on its own, leaving her skin tight and needing a second layer of moisturizer on top.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers describing sensitive skin mostly report no irritation, including one using it daily for six weeks who calls it a sunscreen that finally doesn't upset her easily-irritated skin, though one sensitive, combination, acne-prone reviewer found it left her shinier than she'd like and switched to the tinted version instead.
segments.combination: The one reviewer with combination skin in this set found it required extra effort to blend in without a white cast and left her a bit shiny, ultimately preferring EltaMD's tinted formula instead.

concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers describe the formula as hydrating or moisturizing, but one with dry skin found it left her skin feeling tight and needing a reapplication of moisturizer, and another noted her face felt slightly dry shortly after an initially moisturizing feel.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers report no stinging or irritation, even around the eyes, but two flag concerns worth noting: one describes a severe, long-lasting rash she attributes to what she believes was a counterfeit product rather than the genuine formula, and another reports getting sunburned despite applying it before extended outdoor time.
concerns.oiliness: Reports are mixed: several reviewers praise a genuinely non-greasy, matte finish, but one with an oil-prone T-zone says it left her visibly greasy within an hour, and another with combination skin found it left her shinier than expected.

aspects.libelle: Can leave a white cast on deeper or olive skin tones
Runs thin and watery, less emollient than the cream version
Tube sometimes arrives unsealed or already open
Small tube size relative to the price
Wears well under makeup without pilling

extraits.texte: DANGER. This is a NOT the real thing, it is a knock-off and gave me a HORRIBLE RASH all over my face and neck! The rash got worse and worse even after I stopped using it, for ten more days my face and neck were covered with red bumps that itched like mosquito bites. DO NOT USE! It "looks authentic" at first, but the label is worded differently different from the authentic product on the official Elta MD website. DO NOT USE!!

I am brown toned and about a V on the pitzpatric scale and unfortunately this sheer UV leaves a definite white cast even after 10mins. I have dry skin and was hoping this light fluid would feel comfortable after my moisturiser but I found I had to reapply moisturiser on top again after a while as my skin felt a little tight. Unfortunately I won’t be using this during the day and will try to use it up during outdoor sports when I know it will be washed off soon after.

I don’t know why it’s so hard to find a non greasy sunscreen. Have tried mattifying ones that LOOK powdery but never dry and come off on my clothes. Decided to try this elta md formulation since oily skinned folks like it. I can say that it doesn’t FEEL greasy. However. Even after an hour and a half of letting this stuff absorb I look like a ball of grease. Mind you this is after washing my face and I’m not super oily to start with, just have an oil prone T zone. This oil slick on my face is all elta md not natural face oil. I can’t believe it.

extraits.titre: Lightweight Lotion, But Leaves Me Shiny and Takes Effort To Rub In
extraits.texte: The EltaMD (non-tinted) Sheer Face SPF 50+ is an overall great sunscreen. It comes in a small 1.7oz tube. The white, watergel like texture is lightweight and near odorless. Seems very hydrating. I am over 40, a natural redhead (who is prone to burn, not tan), with sensitive, combination, acne-prone skin. This particular version of EltaMD’s spf is not my favorite though, as this one leaves me looking a hint shiny and does take a little effort to avoid white cast (having to massage it in more thoroughly than what I’m used to). I will likely finish the bottle and move along to EltaMD’s tinted version of this sunscreen. For whatever reason, for me, it has better spreadability and doesn’t leave me looking oily or shiny. That is not to say there is anything wrong with this SPF. I like that it has a high % of zinc oxide (physical blockers) and doesn’t have the telltale old school sunscreen smell of my youth. I also understand zinc oxide is often the culprits for white cast as it requires being milled extra fine. I just don’t want to appear glossy or glowy. I think this is better suited for users with more dry complexions; and (generally) those with sensitive skin.

extraits.titre: Amazing! Great for sensitive skin, doesn't feel greasy, and works perfectly under makeup!
extraits.texte: I've been avoiding sunlight for decades, but occasionally it's inescapable. You'll never find me willingly soaking up the rays, but I do have to walk out to my car in summer, drive somewhere on my lunch hour, etc. I've gotten used to my foundation makeup having some SPF, but when I recently changed formulas, I was surprised to find zero mention of sun protection on the bottle. So off I went in search of a unicorn -- that is, a sunscreen that doesn't irritate my skin, doesn't affect the color or finish of my makeup, doesn't feel greasy, and doesn't smell like a day at the pool. I checked around the web for discussions about the best sunscreen to wear under makeup, and this EltaMD formula kept popping up. The price is definitely more than I would ever spend on something like this, but fortunately it's eligible for FSA, so I was able to put it on that account. I was a little worried about pilling because while some reviewers said it didn't pill at all, others said it pills badly. As for how it turned out for me... It's perfect. My skin is easily irritated, but I've been wearing this sunscreen daily for 6 weeks now, and my skin is happy. It's lightweight and feels like it moisturizes, so I use this instead of a moisturizer each morning, but it doesn't feel oily or greasy at all. It does have a little bit of a white cast to it, but that fades quickly and doesn't change the appearance of my foundation at all. And no, it doesn't make my foundation pill! EltaMD UV Sheer Face Sunscreen Broad-Spectrum SPF 50+ is claimed to be Water Resistant, Mineral Based Sun Protection, Non Greasy, Lightweight Daily Oil Free Zinc Oxide Sunscreen Lotion. Here are my thoughts below, Pros, - non irritating : doesn’t make me tear even applying bear eye lids, eye area - non greasy - non whitening looking : some sunscreen makes my face very powdery, looking like white clown but this sunscreen did great job on blending into my skin tone. - good daily sunscreen even under makeup - nice tube applications for liquid constancy Cons - Dry : although the sunscreen is moisturizing feeling when I apply soon later my face feels slightly dry (your face looks shiny after applying the sunscreen but I think it’s a good thing because my face looks heathy and glowy from it in my option) - high price, $30 - not advertising full ingredients on their page. : I tried to find all the ingredients other than key, active ingredients I simply couldn’t find - doesn’t feel like protecting from sun : I applied this sunscreen before gardening. I still got some redness after being outside. (Apply frequently of course) Overall, I like this sunscreen because this sunscreen has no white cast, no dry pasty texture and goes on nice and smooth. But, the price is higher than other products on the market.

extraits.titre: Close but doesn’t hit the markClose but doesn’t hit the mark
extraits.texte: This sunscreen is probably really good for other people but for me there are several reasons why I wouldn’t reach for it for my daily sunscreen. I will start with the positives -Initially dewy but dries matte!!! A sunscreen that will not make you feel oily (elta sport was wayyyy to shiny for me). Very clean matte finish. -No fragrance -Easy to apply. Grips skin but feels lightweight. I feel very adequately protected from the sun. -High UVA protection with high zinc oxide -water resistant (definetly feels that way) -no eye sting The cons -white cast :/ got my hopes high that it would be invisible or subtle as marketed but it is not. I am an olive toned person and the white cast was too strong for my liking. It initially goes on with a strong white cast that fades slightly after about 2-3 hours. Though there is a saying in the skincare community, any mineral sunscreen will always have a white cast. -Price but there is no surprise there. Elta Md positions themselves as the luxury drug store skin care brand. -The THD (vitamin c) irritates my skin upon application but fades. This is my second time trying to love an Elta Md sunscreen because I love love love hybrid sunscreen formulations. Currently my favorite American hybrid sunscreen is the jack black sun guard. That sunscreen has the most perfect finish, but I highly suspect it has the weakest UVA protection compared to any elta Md sunscreen. Overall I could see this being a holy grail for a pale, oily skin type person. Or anyon
